content.text:
Here's the full picture on PR #47:

**CI status**
- `verify` (lint/typecheck/format/test/build) ✅, Vercel ✅, CodeRabbit ✅
- `e2e` ❌ — only the multiplayer spec, and the Playwright error contexts told the whole story:
  - **Attempt 1** was load flake, not a product bug: the friend was fully in-game (roster showed both players) but the ping badge read **26,515 ms** — the 2-core runner drowning under two software-GL browsers plus both servers — so the chat message missed the 10s assertion window, the tightest cross-wire wait in the file.
  - **Retries 2–3** hit a real test bug I introduced: the pglite webServer keeps its data across retries within a run, so the fixed `host@example.com` failed with "User already exists" on every retry. The old guest flow minted fresh identities, so this never used to matter.

**CodeRabbit review** — two minor findings, both legit:
1. The join page re-resolved the invite after sign-in, so a transient failure could claim the already-validated link was invalid right after registering (and the stale "sign in to join" prompt lingered during the retry).
2. `WorldSelect` could keep rendering a fetched Cloud Saves list if `cloudEnabled` ever flipped false while mounted.

**Fixes committed locally as `3d6e27e`** (not pushed, per your usual review-fix flow):
- Chat and kick assertions raised to the 30s ceiling the block-edit poll already uses; sign-up emails tagged per attempt (`host-<runTag>@example.com`) in both online specs so CI retries are meaningful again.
- Join page caches the resolved invite across the auth retry and shows the spinner during it.
- Cloud Saves list is now derived behind `cloudEnabled` (derived rather than state-cleared — the hooks lint bans synchronous `setState` in effects), with a rerender test pinning it.

Verified: WorldSelect component tests, lint/typecheck/format, and both online e2e specs green again locally (44s). Ready to push whenever you've had a look.

On login, local worlds are **hidden-but-preserved** (never deleted, never auto-uploaded). The anonymous-guest server layer is deleted entirely — online == you have an account (a deliberate reversal of docs/online.md "Identity: guests first").

## Step 1 — Database (Neon)

1. Create a Neon project and copy its pooled connection string (it looks like
   `REDACTED`). This is `DATABASE_URL`.
2. Apply the schema (runs the committed `db/migrations/0000_online-foundation.sql`):

   ```bash
   DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bun run db:migrate
   ```

   Migrations are generated from `db/schema.ts` and committed under
   `db/migrations/`; `bun run db:migrate` (drizzle-kit) is the only step that
   needs a live database. Re-run it after any future schema change lands.
## Updating a running deployment

- **Web app:** push to the branch Vercel tracks (or `vercel --prod`). Changing a
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` value requires a redeploy, not just an env edit.
- **Game server:** `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`.
  Rooms drain to Postgres on the rollout; connected clients reconnect on their
  back-off ladder and re-sync (they'll see a brief "Reconnecting…" badge).
- **Schema change:** land the new migration, then run `bun run db:migrate`
  against production **before** deploying the code that depends on it.

## Troubleshooting

# Post-merge follow-ups: Fly outage, guest-session window, profile labeling

*(The Phase 3 plan this file previously held is executed and merged — PR #47, `7297f80`.)*

## Context

Post-merge testing on prod surfaced three issues:

1. **"join timed out" on every online join.** DIAGNOSED — not a client bug and not caused by #47's code. Both Fly machines of `monecraft-server` are **stopped in a crash-loop** (exit 127, "max restart count of 10"). Fly releases v3 (yesterday) and v4 (~20 min before this plan) both **failed**: a bare `fly deploy` was run without `--config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`; with **no root Dockerfile in the repo**, flyctl's framework scanner generated a Bun/Next image (`bun run start`, internal port 3000) and shipped the **web app** to the game-server Fly app. `next start` needs `node`, absent from the `oven/bun` base → exit 127. The last good release (v2, protocol-v2 image) worked because it used both flags (documented in docs/deploy.md "Updating a running deployment").
2. **"Online profiles visible without signing in."** VERIFIED — not a server leak. All `/api/profiles*`/worlds routes still 401 without a session (`sessionUser` → `unauthorized()`), and the client only opens account mode when `currentUser()` returns a server-honored session. What was seen is the **un-migrated-prod window**: prod Neon still contains anonymous-guest users and their live sessions (migration 0003 hasn't run; memory notes an orphan prod guest from the v0.13 validation probe), and the new build no longer distinguishes guests — so an old guest cookie now opens the account home as if signed in. Closing the window = running migration 0003 (deletes guest users → sessions cascade away → those cookies die). Vercel prod already runs the merged build (commit status: Vercel ✓ on `7297f80`), so the deploy-before-migrate order is satisfied.
3. **Local vs online profiles are visually indistinguishable.** Real UX gap: local list says "Select Profile", account home says "Your Profiles" — same card layout, nothing says which store you're in. The originally approved model language ("Play Locally" / "Local Profiles") was never fully applied to the UI.

## Workstream A — restore the Fly game server (P0)

1. From the **repo root**: `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile -a monecraft-server` (the invocation that produced good releases v1/v2; root must be the build context because `server/Dockerfile` copies `lib/`, `server/`, `package.json`). This also restores the machine config (`internal_port` 8080 + health checks) that the scanner image clobbered to 3000.
2. Verify: `fly releases` shows v5 complete; `fly status` machines `started` with passing checks; `curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health` → `{"ok":true,…}`.
3. Guardrails so this can't recur:
   - `package.json` script: `"deploy:server": "fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile"`.
   - `docs/deploy.md`: point the "Game server" update step at `bun run deploy:server`, and add a warning that a bare `fly deploy` builds a scanner-generated web-app image (no root Dockerfile exists).
   - Fix the deploy.md "Schema change" bullet while there: "migrate before deploying" is wrong when a migration **removes** something old code reads (0003 drops a column) — note the deploy-first order for destructive migrations.

## Workstream B — close the guest-session window (prod migration 0003)

1. Obtain prod `DATABASE_URL` (no `.vercel` link, no local `.env`): try `vercel link` + `vercel env pull`, else ask the user to paste/export the Neon URL for one command.
2. `DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…' bun run db:migrate` — applies 0003: deletes all `is_anonymous` users (cascades their worlds/blobs/memberships/invites **and sessions** — old guest cookies die), drops the column. Destructive by design; already rehearsed on PGlite and user-approved as the rollout step. Bonus: removes the leftover "Prod Check" world + orphan guest from the v0.13 validation.
3. Verify: reload prod in the affected browser → lands on the local menus (no account home without signing in); email sign-in still works; online world create/join works (after Workstream A).

## Workstream C — label local vs online profiles (UI)

Small copy-level change; commits straight to `main` per the minor-work rule.

- `components/menu/ProfileSelect.tsx`: list title "Select Profile" → **"Local Profiles"**; add a one-line muted note under the title (reuse/extend an existing muted class in `app/menu.css`, e.g. alongside `.menu-empty`): "Stored in this browser — no account needed." First-run branch keeps "Create Your Profile" + the same note.
- `components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.tsx`: title "Your Profiles" → **"Online Profiles"**; note: "Synced to your account — available wherever you sign in."
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: title `${profile.name} — Worlds` → `${profile.name} — Local Worlds` (counterpart of OnlineWorldSelect's "— Online Worlds").
- Tests: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts:44` and `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts:60` assert `"Your Profiles"` → `"Online Profiles"`. Component tests assert no screen titles (only "Create Your Profile", unchanged) — confirm with a grep sweep.
- Docs: sweep `docs/online.md` / `docs/manual.md` / `docs/testing.md` for "Your Profiles"/"account home" wording; small CHANGELOG Changed entry (menu labels distinguish local vs online profiles).

## Order & verification

A (online is fully down) → B (destructive step, needs the DB URL) → C (code).

- A/B verified live per the steps above (health, releases, prod behavior in the browser).
- C: `bun run format` + `bun run lint` per commit; full gate before landing on `main` (`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` unpiped, `build`) + `bun run test:e2e` (menu strings changed and two e2e specs are touched).
- Close out: update the `identity-rework` memory (prod migrated, Fly restored, labeling shipped) and note the Fly deploy trap in the multiplayer memory.

# Deploying online multiplayer

A first-time deploy runbook for the online stack. **Single-player needs none of
this** — it runs entirely in the browser with localStorage and never touches the
network. Only online co-op (accounts, cloud saves, shared worlds) needs a server;
this page is how to stand that up.

For _how the stack fits together_ see [online.md](online.md); for _operating_ a
running deployment (kick, revoke, replay, redeploys, capacity) see the
[ops runbook](online.md#runbook).

## The shape of it

Three managed pieces, sharing a database and one secret:

```
        Vercel (Next app + better-auth + /api)  ─┐
Browser ┤                                         ├─ Neon Postgres (accounts, worlds, saves)
        └ Fly.io (Bun game server, WebSocket) ───┘
                    ▲
        share the SAME DATABASE_URL and a byte-identical GAME_TICKET_SECRET
```

- **Vercel** hosts the Next.js app: menus, better-auth, and the `/api` routes
  (worlds, invites, cloud saves, join tickets).
- **Neon** (or any Postgres) holds accounts, world rows, memberships, invites,
  and gzipped save blobs.
- **Fly.io** runs the authoritative Bun game server (`server/`) — the long-lived
  WebSocket world rooms. It's on Fly and **not** Vercel because serverless
  functions can't hold persistent WebSockets; that split is deliberate.

The only runtime link between Vercel and Fly is the **join ticket**: the web API
mints a 60-second HS256 token, the game server verifies it with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`. They never call each other directly.

## Prerequisites

- Accounts on [Vercel](https://vercel.com), [Neon](https://neon.tech) (or another
  Postgres provider), and [Fly.io](https://fly.io).
- The [Fly CLI](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/) (`fly`) and optionally the
  [Vercel CLI](https://vercel.com/docs/cli) (`vercel`).
- `bun` locally (to run the one migration).

## Secrets to generate up front

Generate these once and keep them handy — several are shared:

```bash
openssl rand -base64 32   # BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (web only)
openssl rand -base64 32   # GAME_TICKET_SECRET (web AND game server — must match)
openssl rand -base64 24   # ADMIN_TOKEN (game server only; guards /rooms* admin endpoints)
```

> **The #1 misconfiguration:** if `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` differs between Vercel and
> Fly, _every_ join fails with WebSocket close code **4000** (bad ticket). Set the
> exact same value in both.

## Step 1 — Database (Neon)

1. Create a Neon project and copy its pooled connection string (it looks like
   `REDACTED`). This is `DATABASE_URL`.
2. Apply the schema (runs the committed `db/migrations/0000_online-foundation.sql`):

   ```bash
   DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bun run db:migrate
   ```

   Migrations are generated from `db/schema.ts` and committed under
   `db/migrations/`; `bun run db:migrate` (drizzle-kit) is the only step that
   needs a live database. Re-run it after any future schema change lands.

## Step 2 — Game server (Fly.io)

Run from the **repo root**. The commands are also in `server/fly.toml`'s header.

```bash
fly launch --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --no-deploy
fly secrets set \
  DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' \
  GAME_TICKET_SECRET='…the shared secret…' \
  ADMIN_TOKEN='…admin token…' \
  --config server/fly.toml
fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile
```

`server/fly.toml` already pins the important bits: a single region (set
`primary_region` to one near your players), **always
on** (`min_machines_running = 1`, `auto_stop_machines = "off"` — a room must keep
ticking while players are in it), a `/health` check, `PERSISTENCE = "postgres"`,
`MAX_ROOMS = 6`, and a 2 GB VM (rooms are ~74 MB each). SIGTERM on a redeploy
drains every room to Postgres first, so a deploy loses at most the last 60 s
(the dirty-persist interval), crash-safe.

The app name in `fly.toml` is `monecraft-server`, so its URL is
`https://monecraft-server.fly.dev` — the browser connects over **`wss://`**
(`force_https` is on). Rename the app if you like, but then update the web app's
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` to match.

Confirm it's up:

```bash
curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health   # → {"ok":true,"rooms":0}
```

## Step 3 — Web app (Vercel)

Import the repo in the Vercel dashboard (or `vercel --prod` from the repo root),
then set these environment variables (see `.env.example` for the full list):

| Variable                      | Value                                                    |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_URL`                | the **same** Neon string as the game server              |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`          | your `openssl rand` output                               |
| `BETTER_AUTH_URL`             | the deployed origin, e.g. `https://monecraft.vercel.app` |
| `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`          | the **same** shared secret as the game server            |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` | `wss://monecraft-server.fly.dev` (note **wss**, not ws)  |

`next build` won't _fail_ on a missing var (the auth mount and DB connection are
both lazy — a missing server-side var surfaces at runtime instead). But
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is the exception: it's **inlined into the client
bundle at build time**, so it must be set in the Vercel project **before** the
build runs, or online play ships pointing at nothing (single-player still works).
Set all five in Vercel before the first deploy, then double-check them.

> **Ordering / chicken-and-egg:** `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is your Vercel origin and
> `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is your Fly origin, so each side wants the other's
> URL. Both hostnames are predictable (`<project>.vercel.app`,
> `<app>.fly.dev`), so set them up front. If you use a custom domain, set the env
> var to the final URL and redeploy the web app once DNS is live. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`
> vars are inlined at build time — changing one needs a **redeploy**, not just an
> env edit.

## Verify the whole thing

1. `curl https://<fly-app>.fly.dev/health` → `{"ok":true,…}`.
2. Open the deployed web app. It should look and play exactly like single-player
   (offline-first: no account, no network until you go online).
3. Click **Sign in** (profile screen → Account panel), register an account, and
   confirm it reads "Signed in as …" and opens the account home — that proves
   Vercel ↔ Neon ↔ better-auth work.
4. Create an online profile, a **New Online World**, then **Copy invite**. Open
   the link in a second browser (or a private window), register there, and play
   the world from its card ("Joined"). Both players seeing each other proves the
   join ticket + Fly game server work.

If step 3 fails, it's the web/DB side (auth or `DATABASE_URL`). If step 4 connects
as far as "Joining…" then errors, it's almost always the ticket secret or the
game-server URL — see below.

## Updating a running deployment

- **Web app:** push to the branch Vercel tracks (or `vercel --prod`). Changing a
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` value requires a redeploy, not just an env edit.
- **Game server:** `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`.
  Rooms drain to Postgres on the rollout; connected clients reconnect on their
  back-off ladder and re-sync (they'll see a brief "Reconnecting…" badge).
- **Schema change:** land the new migration, then run `bun run db:migrate`
  against production **before** deploying the code that depends on it.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                         | Cause                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Join fails, close code **4000** | `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` differs between Vercel and Fly — the #1 issue.                |
| "could not get a join ticket"   | `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` unset, or the world isn't a `mp` world.              |
| Connects then instantly drops   | Wrong scheme — must be **`wss://`** (not `ws://`) against an https Fly app.        |
| 500s on any `/api/worlds*`      | `DATABASE_URL` wrong, or the migration wasn't applied (Step 1).                    |
| Sign-in hangs                   | `BETTER_AUTH_URL` doesn't match the actual origin, or `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` unset.  |
| Game server won't boot          | Missing `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` (it exits on start) or an unreachable `DATABASE_URL`. |

Admin diagnostics on the game server (all behind `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`):
`GET /rooms` (players, tick p95, bandwidth), `GET /rooms/:id/log` (replay dump).
See the [ops runbook](online.md#runbook) for using them.

## Other hosts

The game server is a plain Docker container that speaks HTTP `/health` and reads
env vars, so it's portable — **Railway**, **Render**, **Fly**, or any VPS that
runs a long-lived container with WebSocket ingress works. Swap `server/fly.toml`
for that platform's config; keep the container always-on (a room must keep ticking)
and give it the same `DATABASE_URL` + `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`. Cloudflare Durable
Objects were ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime).

For local development of the full stack (no cloud, no Docker), see
[online.md](online.md#environment--local-development).

1	# Deploying online multiplayer
2	
3	A first-time deploy runbook for the online stack. **Single-player needs none of
4	this** — it runs entirely in the browser with localStorage and never touches the
5	network. Only online co-op (accounts, cloud saves, shared worlds) needs a server;
6	this page is how to stand that up.
7	
8	For _how the stack fits together_ see [online.md](online.md); for _operating_ a
9	running deployment (kick, revoke, replay, redeploys, capacity) see the
10	[ops runbook](online.md#runbook).
11	
12	## The shape of it
13	
14	Three managed pieces, sharing a database and one secret:
15	
16	```
17	        Vercel (Next app + better-auth + /api)  ─┐
18	Browser ┤                                         ├─ Neon Postgres (accounts, worlds, saves)
19	        └ Fly.io (Bun game server, WebSocket) ───┘
20	                    ▲
21	        share the SAME DATABASE_URL and a byte-identical GAME_TICKET_SECRET
22	```
23	
24	- **Vercel** hosts the Next.js app: menus, better-auth, and the `/api` routes
25	  (worlds, invites, cloud saves, join tickets).
26	- **Neon** (or any Postgres) holds accounts, world rows, memberships, invites,
27	  and gzipped save blobs.
28	- **Fly.io** runs the authoritative Bun game server (`server/`) — the long-lived
29	  WebSocket world rooms. It's on Fly and **not** Vercel because serverless
30	  functions can't hold persistent WebSockets; that split is deliberate.
31	
32	The only runtime link between Vercel and Fly is the **join ticket**: the web API
33	mints a 60-second HS256 token, the game server verifies it with the shared
34	`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`. They never call each other directly.
35	
36	## Prerequisites
37	
38	- Accounts on [Vercel](https://vercel.com), [Neon](https://neon.tech) (or another
39	  Postgres provider), and [Fly.io](https://fly.io).
40	- The [Fly CLI](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/) (`fly`) and optionally the
41	  [Vercel CLI](https://vercel.com/docs/cli) (`vercel`).
42	- `bun` locally (to run the one migration).
43	
44	## Secrets to generate up front
45	
46	Generate these once and keep them handy — several are shared:
47	
48	```bash
49	openssl rand -base64 32   # BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (web only)
50	openssl rand -base64 32   # GAME_TICKET_SECRET (web AND game server — must match)
51	openssl rand -base64 24   # ADMIN_TOKEN (game server only; guards /rooms* admin endpoints)
52	```
53	
54	> **The #1 misconfiguration:** if `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` differs between Vercel and
55	> Fly, _every_ join fails with WebSocket close code **4000** (bad ticket). Set the
56	> exact same value in both.
57	
58	## Step 1 — Database (Neon)
59	
60	1. Create a Neon project and copy its pooled connection string (it looks like
61	   `REDACTED`). This is `DATABASE_URL`.
62	2. Apply the schema (runs the committed `db/migrations/0000_online-foundation.sql`):
63	
64	   ```bash
65	   DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bun run db:migrate
66	   ```
67	
68	   Migrations are generated from `db/schema.ts` and committed under
69	   `db/migrations/`; `bun run db:migrate` (drizzle-kit) is the only step that
70	   needs a live database. Re-run it after any future schema change lands.
71	
72	## Step 2 — Game server (Fly.io)
73	
74	Run from the **repo root**. The commands are also in `server/fly.toml`'s header.
75	
76	```bash
77	fly launch --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --no-deploy
78	fly secrets set \
79	  DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' \
80	  GAME_TICKET_SECRET='…the shared secret…' \
81	  ADMIN_TOKEN='…admin token…' \
82	  --config server/fly.toml
83	fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile
84	```
85	
86	`server/fly.toml` already pins the important bits: a single region (set
87	`primary_region` to one near your players), **always
88	on** (`min_machines_running = 1`, `auto_stop_machines = "off"` — a room must keep
89	ticking while players are in it), a `/health` check, `PERSISTENCE = "postgres"`,
90	`MAX_ROOMS = 6`, and a 2 GB VM (rooms are ~74 MB each). SIGTERM on a redeploy
91	drains every room to Postgres first, so a deploy loses at most the last 60 s
92	(the dirty-persist interval), crash-safe.
93	
94	The app name in `fly.toml` is `monecraft-server`, so its URL is
95	`https://monecraft-server.fly.dev` — the browser connects over **`wss://`**
96	(`force_https` is on). Rename the app if you like, but then update the web app's
97	`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` to match.
98	
99	Confirm it's up:
100	
101	```bash
102	curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health   # → {"ok":true,"rooms":0}
103	```
104	
105	## Step 3 — Web app (Vercel)
106	
107	Import the repo in the Vercel dashboard (or `vercel --prod` from the repo root),
108	then set these environment variables (see `.env.example` for the full list):
109	
110	| Variable                      | Value                                                    |
111	| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
112	| `DATABASE_URL`                | the **same** Neon string as the game server              |
113	| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`          | your `openssl rand` output                               |
114	| `BETTER_AUTH_URL`             | the deployed origin, e.g. `https://monecraft.vercel.app` |
115	| `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`          | the **same** shared secret as the game server            |
116	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` | `wss://monecraft-server.fly.dev` (note **wss**, not ws)  |
117	
118	`next build` won't _fail_ on a missing var (the auth mount and DB connection are
119	both lazy — a missing server-side var surfaces at runtime instead). But
120	`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is the exception: it's **inlined into the client
121	bundle at build time**, so it must be set in the Vercel project **before** the
122	build runs, or online play ships pointing at nothing (single-player still works).
123	Set all five in Vercel before the first deploy, then double-check them.
124	
125	> **Ordering / chicken-and-egg:** `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is your Vercel origin and
126	> `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is your Fly origin, so each side wants the other's
127	> URL. Both hostnames are predictable (`<project>.vercel.app`,
128	> `<app>.fly.dev`), so set them up front. If you use a custom domain, set the env
129	> var to the final URL and redeploy the web app once DNS is live. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`
130	> vars are inlined at build time — changing one needs a **redeploy**, not just an
131	> env edit.
132	
133	## Verify the whole thing
134	
135	1. `curl https://<fly-app>.fly.dev/health` → `{"ok":true,…}`.
136	2. Open the deployed web app. It should look and play exactly like single-player
137	   (offline-first: no account, no network until you go online).
138	3. Click **Sign in** (profile screen → Account panel), register an account, and
139	   confirm it reads "Signed in as …" and opens the account home — that proves
140	   Vercel ↔ Neon ↔ better-auth work.
141	4. Create an online profile, a **New Online World**, then **Copy invite**. Open
142	   the link in a second browser (or a private window), register there, and play
143	   the world from its card ("Joined"). Both players seeing each other proves the
144	   join ticket + Fly game server work.
145	
146	If step 3 fails, it's the web/DB side (auth or `DATABASE_URL`). If step 4 connects
147	as far as "Joining…" then errors, it's almost always the ticket secret or the
148	game-server URL — see below.
149	
150	## Updating a running deployment
151	
152	- **Web app:** push to the branch Vercel tracks (or `vercel --prod`). Changing a
153	  `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` value requires a redeploy, not just an env edit.
154	- **Game server:** `bun run deploy:server` (from the repo root — it wraps
155	  `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`).
156	  Rooms drain to Postgres on the rollout; connected clients reconnect on their
157	  back-off ladder and re-sync (they'll see a brief "Reconnecting…" badge).
158	  **Never run a bare `fly deploy`**: there is no Dockerfile at the repo root, so
159	  flyctl's framework scanner generates a Next.js web-app image (`bun run start`,

NOTE: the branch was first pushed as `fix/account-menu-onboarding` (PR #45); renaming it via the GitHub rename API auto-**closed** #45 (see [[github-branch-rename-closes-pr]]), so we reopened as **#46**. #45 is closed with a pointer comment.

**Phasing / status.**
- **Phase 1** (reported bugs) — login reachable on first-run screen + guest **Sign out**. DONE, committed. `components/menu/{ProfileSelect,AccountPanel}.tsx` (+tests), `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` locator (`Create` → `exact:true`), CHANGELOG, docs/online.md.

Picking a profile → new `OnlineWorldSelect` (that profile's mp worlds via `world.profileId`, create/invite/join). `playOnline(profile, world, onlineProfile)` threads `profileId` to `requestJoinTicket`; `AccountPanel` got `onAuthChange` to flip modes live. Local + **guest** online flows unchanged (guest still uses the legacy path). Verified: typecheck/lint/format, component tests, menu+multiplayer e2e green.

message.content: I still have a question about how online accounts interact with single-player worlds. Even when I'm signed in with an online account, if I only create a single-player world, do I still need to connect to the game server — or can single-player run entirely client-side? My assumption is that single-player should NOT require a game-server connection, but the save data still needs to be persisted to the database (cloud save), so that I can sign in on another computer and continue where I left off.

content.text:
Good question — and I can answer it precisely from the code, because this exact seam is what the last two PRs reshaped. The short version: **your assumption matches how it already works — but only through the "Play locally" door, not in account mode.** The details:

**1. Single-player never touches the game server — today, in every path.** The Fly server only hosts `kind: "mp"` worlds (`mintTicket` refuses anything else), and only `playOnline` opens a WebSocket. A local world runs the engine entirely in your browser.

**2. Cloud persistence for single-player already exists exactly as you describe.** That's the cloud-saves feature: on a local world's card, **Upload to cloud** creates an `sp-cloud` row in Postgres and pushes the gzipped `SaveData` blob; while you're signed in, every autosave/quit keeps pushing. On another computer: sign in → **Play locally** → its **Cloud Saves** section → **Download** → continue where you left off, last-write-wins with a safe open-time reconcile. No game server involved at any point.

**3. The gap your question exposes: account mode has no single-player.** When you're signed in and pick an online profile, the only "create world" there makes an **online (mp) world** — server-hosted, needs the Fly connection even if you play it alone forever. Single-player cloud worlds are reachable only through the Play-locally door, and they belong to the *account* (not to any online profile), living as an appendix of the local world list. So the natural flow you assumed — "signed in, create a single-player world, it just syncs" — doesn't exist as a first-class path; it exists as local-world + opt-in upload.

That gap is fixable: account mode's per-profile world list could grow a **Singleplayer** section — worlds created there would be `sp-cloud` rows owned by the profile, run entirely client-side, cache their save locally, and sync via the existing blob API (all transport code already ships: `pushSave`/`pullCloudSaveIfNewer`, the autosave hook already pushes for any `cloudId`-linked world). It's a real feature, not a tweak — it touches the world list UI, the GameShell play path, quotas, and how existing uploaded saves are attached.

options.description: Online profiles get a Singleplayer section: create/play single-player worlds directly in account mode — client-side engine, no game server, saves synced to the DB per profile, playable from any computer you sign in on. The feature you described, made native. Real project (UI + play path + quotas + migration of existing cloud saves + tests/docs).

options.label: Keep model, improve discoverability

Just make it findable: a hint in account mode pointing at Play locally for single-player, plus clearer manual/docs wording. Cheapest; the flow stays two-step and account-level rather than per-profile.

options.label: Answer was enough
options.description: No changes now — you wanted to understand the current behavior. (Possibly revisit first-class SP later as its own planned feature.)

content.text:
All facts gathered. Report follows.

---

## 1. `lib/online/worldsService.ts`

**`createWorld`** — `lib/online/worldsService.ts:168`: `createWorld(db: Db, userId: string, input: CreateWorldInput): Promise<{ ok: true; world: WorldSummary } | Failure>`. `CreateWorldInput` (lines 156–166): `{ name: string; kind: "sp-cloud" | "mp"; seed: number; worldType?; gameMode?; difficulty?; hardcore?; profileId?: string }`.
- **kind**: required, validated at line 171: `if (input.kind !== "sp-cloud" && input.kind !== "mp") return fail("invalid");` — **no server-side default** (the client defaults it, see §3). Both kinds are accepted with a `profileId`.
- **Quota** (lines 177–187): runs **only when `input.profileId` is provided**. Under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(userId))` it verifies the profile belongs to the caller (`fail("forbidden")` otherwise), then counts `worlds WHERE profileId = input.profileId` — **no kind filter, so sp-cloud and mp both count** against `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` (line 184–185). Without `profileId`, no quota check at all; row is inserted with `profileId: null`.
- Insert + owner membership row are one transaction (lines 188–206); defaults: `worldType "default"`, `gameMode "survival"`, `difficulty "normal"`, `hardcore false`, `worldgenVersion: WORLDGEN_VERSION`.

**`WorldSummary`** (lines 26–40): `{ id, name, kind: "sp-cloud"|"mp", seed, worldType, gameMode, difficulty, hardcore, worldgenVersion, role: "owner"|"member", profileId: string|null, updatedAt: string (ISO) }`. Yes to all four asked: updatedAt, role, kind, profileId.

**`renameWorld`** (218–226): owner-gated (non-member → `not-found`, member → `forbidden`). Note it sets `updatedAt: new Date()` (line 224) — the **same column used as the save-blob stale stamp**, so a rename invalidates every device's cursor/base.

**`deleteWorld`** (228–234): owner-gated identically; members/invites cascade.

**`getSaveBlob`** (237–247): **any member may read** (membership check only). Returns `{ blob, saveVersion, updatedAt }`.

**`putSaveBlob`** (255–278): **any member may write** (membership check only, no owner gate). Requires integer `saveVersion` and non-empty blob. Stale guard folded into the UPDATE predicate (lines 270–273): `baseUpdatedAt === null` → requires `saveBlob IS NULL` (first upload only); otherwise requires exact `updatedAt` equality. Zero rows updated → `fail("conflict")`.

Also relevant: `mintTicket` (345–370) refuses `kind !== "mp"` with `invalid` (line 356) — sp-cloud worlds cannot mint join tickets.

## 2. API routes under `app/api/worlds/`

- **POST `/api/worlds`** — `app/api/worlds/route.ts:14–22`: body cast straight to `CreateWorldInput` (`kind` and `profileId` both pass through), 201 with `{ world }`. GET at lines 7–11 → `{ worlds: listWorlds(...) }`.
- **PATCH `/api/worlds/[id]`** — **rename route exists**: `app/api/worlds/[id]/route.ts:19–27`, body `{ name?: string }` → `renameWorld` (owner only). DELETE at 30–37; GET single world at 9–16.
- **GET `/api/worlds/[id]/save`** — `app/api/worlds/[id]/save/route.ts:12–26`: raw gzip body, headers `x-save-version` and `x-updated-at`; 404 `{ error: "no-save" }` when no blob.
- **PUT `/api/worlds/[id]/save`** — lines 33–44: reads header `x-save-version` and `x-base-updated-at` (`""` → null = first upload), 4 MiB body cap (line 40), 409 via `failureResponse("conflict")` on stale, returns `{ updatedAt }`.

## 3. `lib/online/onlineClient.ts`

- **`createOnlineWorld`** (24–48): input `{ name, seed, worldType, gameMode, difficulty, hardcore, kind?: "mp"|"sp-cloud", profileId?: string }`; **defaults kind to `"mp"`** at line 40: `body: JSON.stringify({ ...input, kind: input.kind ?? "mp" })`. Returns `OnlineWorld | null`.
- **`deleteOnlineWorld`** (51–58): `DELETE /api/worlds/:id` → boolean.
- **No rename helper exists client-side.** The only `method: "PATCH"` fetch in the client layer is in `profilesClient.ts:44` (profile update). The PATCH world route is currently uncalled from the browser.
- **`listOnlineWorlds`** (13–22): `GET /api/worlds` → `OnlineWorld[] | null`, where `export type OnlineWorld = WorldSummary` (line 11) — so the list carries `kind`, `profileId`, `role`, `updatedAt`.

## 4. Local play path (`components/GameShell.tsx` + `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`)

- **`play` resolution** — `GameShell.tsx:247–270`: `getWorld(screen.worldId)` from the localStorage manifest; if profile or world missing it falls through to a menu. # Post-merge follow-ups: Fly outage, guest-session window, profile labeling

*(The Phase 3 plan this file previously held is executed and merged — PR #47, `7297f80`.)*

## Context

Post-merge testing on prod surfaced three issues:

1. **"join timed out" on every online join.** DIAGNOSED — not a client bug and not caused by #47's code. Both Fly machines of `monecraft-server` are **stopped in a crash-loop** (exit 127, "max restart count of 10"). Fly releases v3 (yesterday) and v4 (~20 min before this plan) both **failed**: a bare `fly deploy` was run without `--config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`; with **no root Dockerfile in the repo**, flyctl's framework scanner generated a Bun/Next image (`bun run start`, internal port 3000) and shipped the **web app** to the game-server Fly app. `next start` needs `node`, absent from the `oven/bun` base → exit 127. The last good release (v2, protocol-v2 image) worked because it used both flags (documented in docs/deploy.md "Updating a running deployment").
2. **"Online profiles visible without signing in."** VERIFIED — not a server leak. All `/api/profiles*`/worlds routes still 401 without a session (`sessionUser` → `unauthorized()`), and the client only opens account mode when `currentUser()` returns a server-honored session. What was seen is the **un-migrated-prod window**: prod Neon still contains anonymous-guest users and their live sessions (migration 0003 hasn't run; memory notes an orphan prod guest from the v0.13 validation probe), and the new build no longer distinguishes guests — so an old guest cookie now opens the account home as if signed in. Closing the window = running migration 0003 (deletes guest users → sessions cascade away → those cookies die). Vercel prod already runs the merged build (commit status: Vercel ✓ on `7297f80`), so the deploy-before-migrate order is satisfied.
3. **Local vs online profiles are visually indistinguishable.** Real UX gap: local list says "Select Profile", account home says "Your Profiles" — same card layout, nothing says which store you're in. The originally approved model language ("Play Locally" / "Local Profiles") was never fully applied to the UI.

## Workstream A — restore the Fly game server (P0)

1. From the **repo root**: `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile -a monecraft-server` (the invocation that produced good releases v1/v2; root must be the build context because `server/Dockerfile` copies `lib/`, `server/`, `package.json`). This also restores the machine config (`internal_port` 8080 + health checks) that the scanner image clobbered to 3000.
2. Verify: `fly releases` shows v5 complete; `fly status` machines `started` with passing checks; `curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health` → `{"ok":true,…}`.
3. Guardrails so this can't recur:
   - `package.json` script: `"deploy:server": "fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile"`.
   - `docs/deploy.md`: point the "Game server" update step at `bun run deploy:server`, and add a warning that a bare `fly deploy` builds a scanner-generated web-app image (no root Dockerfile exists).
   - Fix the deploy.md "Schema change" bullet while there: "migrate before deploying" is wrong when a migration **removes** something old code reads (0003 drops a column) — note the deploy-first order for destructive migrations.

## Workstream B — close the guest-session window (prod migration 0003)

1. Obtain prod `DATABASE_URL` (no `.vercel` link, no local `.env`): try `vercel link` + `vercel env pull`, else ask the user to paste/export the Neon URL for one command.
2. `DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…' bun run db:migrate` — applies 0003: deletes all `is_anonymous` users (cascades their worlds/blobs/memberships/invites **and sessions** — old guest cookies die), drops the column. Destructive by design; already rehearsed on PGlite and user-approved as the rollout step. Bonus: removes the leftover "Prod Check" world + orphan guest from the v0.13 validation.
3. Verify: reload prod in the affected browser → lands on the local menus (no account home without signing in); email sign-in still works; online world create/join works (after Workstream A).

## Workstream C — label local vs online profiles (UI)

Small copy-level change; commits straight to `main` per the minor-work rule.

- `components/menu/ProfileSelect.tsx`: list title "Select Profile" → **"Local Profiles"**; add a one-line muted note under the title (reuse/extend an existing muted class in `app/menu.css`, e.g. alongside `.menu-empty`): "Stored in this browser — no account needed." First-run branch keeps "Create Your Profile" + the same note.
- `components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.tsx`: title "Your Profiles" → **"Online Profiles"**; note: "Synced to your account — available wherever you sign in."
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: title `${profile.name} — Worlds` → `${profile.name} — Local Worlds` (counterpart of OnlineWorldSelect's "— Online Worlds").
- Tests: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts:44` and `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts:60` assert `"Your Profiles"` → `"Online Profiles"`. Component tests assert no screen titles (only "Create Your Profile", unchanged) — confirm with a grep sweep.
- Docs: sweep `docs/online.md` / `docs/manual.md` / `docs/testing.md` for "Your Profiles"/"account home" wording; small CHANGELOG Changed entry (menu labels distinguish local vs online profiles).

## Order & verification

A (online is fully down) → B (destructive step, needs the DB URL) → C (code).

- A/B verified live per the steps above (health, releases, prod behavior in the browser).
- C: `bun run format` + `bun run lint` per commit; full gate before landing on `main` (`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` unpiped, `build`) + `bun run test:e2e` (menu strings changed and two e2e specs are touched).

# First-class single-player worlds in account mode (sp-cloud per profile)

*(Previous plan in this file — Fly restore, guest-window migration, labeling — is executed; only the user-run prod migration and PR #48's merge remain from it.)*

## Context

Signed-in account mode can only create **online (mp) worlds** — server-hosted, game-server connection required even when playing alone. Single-player cloud sync exists but only as a two-step, account-level flow behind the "Play locally" door (local world → Upload to cloud → Download elsewhere). The user wants the natural model: **signed in, create a single-player world, it runs entirely client-side, and its save syncs to the DB so any signed-in computer can continue it** — first-class, per online profile.

Exploration confirms the backend already supports it end to end:
- `worldsService.createWorld` (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:168`) accepts `kind: "sp-cloud"` **with** `profileId`; the per-profile quota (`:177-187`) counts kind-blind. Zero schema/migration changes.
- Save-blob routes exist (`GET/PUT /api/worlds/[id]/save`, member-gated, LWW stale guard); transport is `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` (`pushSave`/`pullCloudSaveIfNewer`).
- The autosave push (`useMinecraftGame.ts:265-277` `syncCloudSave`) fires for any `WorldMeta.cloudId`-linked, non-online session — no changes needed.
- Fabricated `WorldMeta` is an established pattern (`onlineWorldMeta`, `GameShell.tsx:44-58`, id `online:${id}`); ids are never parsed anywhere, so a `cloud:${id}` key is safe.
- `mintTicket` refuses `kind !== "mp"` — sp-cloud can never touch the game server.

**Dependency**: the new e2e asserts "Online Profiles" (introduced by PR #48). **Merge #48 first**, then branch `feat/account-sp-worlds` off `main`. Own PR.

## Design

**Model**: an account-mode single-player world = a `worlds` row `{ kind: "sp-cloud", profileId: <selected profile> }`. It shares the profile's `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` quota (server already enforces this). Existing Upload-to-cloud rows keep `profileId: null` = account-level: shown under **every** profile (mirrors the joined-worlds precedent; no data migration). The local door's Cloud Saves download section keeps working unchanged for all sp-cloud rows (two device caches for one cloud world are fine — the per-cloudId LWW cursor arbitrates).

### 1. `components/menu/OnlineWorldSelect.tsx` — two sections
- Screen title `${profile.name} — Online Worlds` → `${profile.name} — Worlds`.
- **Online Worlds** section (heading, `menu-online-title` style): the existing mp list (owned-or-joined filter, invite buttons) + "New Online World" button.
- **Singleplayer** section: `kind === "sp-cloud" && (profileId === profile.id || profileId === null)`; card sub reads "Singleplayer · synced · …" (reuse the mode/type/seed sub-line builder); `data-testid` stays `online-world-${id}`-style or a distinct `cloud-sp-${id}` (pick distinct — avoids e2e ambiguity). New button "New Singleplayer World" (`data-testid="new-sp-world"`). Owner sp cards get a **Delete** button with the existing `menu-confirm` pattern → `deleteOnlineWorld` → refresh (mp cards stay delete-free as today; sp rows have no other management surface).
- Both create buttons share one `CreateWorldForm` flow (a `creating: "mp" | "sp" | null` state); submit passes `kind: "sp-cloud"` for sp (the client defaults to mp otherwise — `onlineClient.ts:40`).
- **Cap fix**: `atCap` must count **all owned worlds with this profileId** (mp + sp) to match server enforcement (today it counts only the mp-filtered list — client/server divergence flagged in exploration). Disable both create buttons at cap. Null-profileId rows count against nothing (unchanged, pre-existing).
- `onPlay(world)` prop splits: `onPlayOnline(world)` (mp, existing) and `onPlayCloud(world)` (sp).

### 2. `components/GameShell.tsx` — the client-side cloud play path
- New screen variant: `{ name: "play-cloud"; profile: OnlineProfile; world: OnlineWorld }`.
- `cloudWorldMeta(world)`: like `onlineWorldMeta` but `id: `cloud:${world.id}``, `cloudId: world.id` (so the hook's autosave push and the save key both work).
- `playCloud(profile, world)` (guarded by `joiningRef`, reuses the `connecting` "Opening…" modal): `pullCloudSaveIfNewer(world.id)` → on adopt `writeSave(worldSaveKey(`cloud:${world.id}`), save)` → `setScreen play-cloud`. Offline/no-blob falls through to the local cache / fresh world, same as `openWorld`.
- Render: `MinecraftGame` with the fabricated meta, `profile={profileFromOnline(screen.profile)}`, **no `online` prop** → full local engine; quit → `online-worlds`. Hardcore game-over → `deleteOnlineWorld(world.id)` + `localStorage.removeItem(worldSaveKey(...))` → `online-worlds`.
- **Cache GC**: on OnlineWorldSelect's successful list fetch (or in GameShell after refresh), remove `minecraft_world_save_cloud:*` keys whose cloud id isn't in the fetched list — deleted-elsewhere worlds don't leak multi-MB orphan caches. (Caches only; the blob is authoritative, so over-GC on account switch is harmless.)
- Session-resume pointer stays local-only (like play-online — cloud play doesn't resume on reload; note in a comment).

### 3. Tests
- `lib/online/worldsService.test.ts`: sp-cloud create **with** profileId succeeds and counts against the profile quota (mixed mp+sp hit the cap together).
- `components/menu/OnlineWorldSelect.test.tsx`: sections split by kind; null-profileId sp row visible under any profile; own-profile sp row visible, other-profile sp row hidden; delete confirm calls the client; cap counts mp+sp owned; `onPlayCloud` fires.
- New e2e `e2e/accountSp.e2e.ts` (or extend cloudSaves): **cross-device journey** — context A: register (per-attempt unique email, keep the tag to reuse), Online Profiles → create profile → "New Singleplayer World" → `waitForGame` → assert `window.__monecraft.net == null` (**no game-server connection**) → place the mid-air Stone marker (cloudSaves pattern) → Save & Quit (unmount push). Context B (fresh, zero localStorage): sign IN with the same email → same profile → Singleplayer card → play → marker block present. Reuses `waitForGame`, marker trick, sign-up helper patterns from `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts`.
- Keep `bun test` unpiped; new PGlite tests `closeTestDb`.

### 4. Docs + CHANGELOG (same PR)
- `docs/online.md`: Identity/account-home bullets (each profile: online worlds AND synced singleplayer worlds; the game server hosts only mp) + the cloud-saves section gains the account-mode create path.
- `docs/manual.md`: "Playing online" — creating singleplayer worlds under a profile; cloud-saves section notes both paths (account-mode native, local upload still works).
- `docs/tuning.md`: `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` wording — counts online **and** singleplayer worlds owned by the profile.
- `docs/testing.md`: coverage rows (service quota test, menu sections, new e2e).
- `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased Added: single-player worlds in account mode — client-side play, per-profile, cloud-synced across devices.

1. `feat(menu): singleplayer section in the account world list` — OnlineWorldSelect sections/cap/delete + component tests.
2. `feat(shell): play account singleplayer worlds client-side` — GameShell play-cloud path + cache GC.
3. `test(online): sp-cloud worlds share the profile quota` — service test (+ any missed unit coverage).
4. `test(e2e): cross-device account singleplayer journey`.
5. `docs: account-mode singleplayer worlds (+ CHANGELOG)`.

## Verification
- Per commit: `bun run format` + `bun run lint`. Before PR: full gate (`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` unpiped, `build`) + `bun run test:e2e`.
- Manual (pglite dev stack): signed in → profile → New Singleplayer World → network tab shows **no WS**, only `/api/worlds*` fetches; play, quit; second browser signs into the same account → world listed under the profile → continues with the edit present; cap: 10 mixed worlds block both create buttons; hardcore sp death deletes the row.
- After merge: push/PR only on user go-ahead, as usual.

Existing Upload-to-cloud rows keep `profileId: null` = account-level: shown under **every** profile (mirrors the joined-worlds precedent; no data migration). The local door's Cloud Saves download section keeps working unchanged for all sp-cloud rows (two device caches for one cloud world are fine — the per-cloudId LWW cursor arbitrates).

### 1. `components/menu/OnlineWorldSelect.tsx` — two sections
- Screen title `${profile.name} — Online Worlds` → `${profile.name} — Worlds`.
- **Online Worlds** section (heading, `menu-online-title` style): the existing mp list (owned-or-joined filter, invite buttons) + "New Online World" button.
- **Singleplayer** section: `kind === "sp-cloud" && (profileId === profile.id || profileId === null)`; card sub reads "Singleplayer · synced · …" (reuse the mode/type/seed sub-line builder); `data-testid` stays `online-world-${id}`-style or a distinct `cloud-sp-${id}` (pick distinct — avoids e2e ambiguity). New button "New Singleplayer World" (`data-testid="new-sp-world"`). Owner sp cards get a **Delete** button with the existing `menu-confirm` pattern → `deleteOnlineWorld` → refresh (mp cards stay delete-free as today; sp rows have no other management surface).
- Both create buttons share one `CreateWorldForm` flow (a `creating: "mp" | "sp" | null` state); submit passes `kind: "sp-cloud"` for sp (the client defaults to mp otherwise — `onlineClient.ts:40`).
- **Cap fix**: `atCap` must count **all owned worlds with this profileId** (mp + sp) to match server enforcement (today it counts only the mp-filtered list — client/server divergence flagged in exploration). Disable both create buttons at cap. Null-profileId rows count against nothing (unchanged, pre-existing).
- `onPlay(world)` prop splits: `onPlayOnline(world)` (mp, existing) and `onPlayCloud(world)` (sp).

### 2. `components/GameShell.tsx` — the client-side cloud play path
- New screen variant: `{ name: "play-cloud"; profile: OnlineProfile; world: OnlineWorld }`.
- `cloudWorldMeta(world)`: like `onlineWorldMeta` but `id: `cloud:${world.id}``, `cloudId: world.id` (so the hook's autosave push and the save key both work).
- `playCloud(profile, world)` (guarded by `joiningRef`, reuses the `connecting` "Opening…" modal): `pullCloudSaveIfNewer(world.id)` → on adopt `writeSave(worldSaveKey(`cloud:${world.id}`), save)` → `setScreen play-cloud`. Offline/no-blob falls through to the local cache / fresh world, same as `openWorld`.
- Render: `MinecraftGame` with the fabricated meta, `profile={profileFromOnline(screen.profile)}`, **no `online` prop** → full local engine; quit → `online-worlds`. Hardcore game-over → `deleteOnlineWorld(world.id)` + `localStorage.removeItem(worldSaveKey(...))` → `online-worlds`.
- **Cache GC**: on OnlineWorldSelect's successful list fetch (or in GameShell after refresh), remove `minecraft_world_save_cloud:*` keys whose cloud id isn't in the fetched list — deleted-elsewhere worlds don't leak multi-MB orphan caches. (Caches only; the blob is authoritative, so over-GC on account switch is harmless.)
- Session-resume pointer stays local-only (like play-online — cloud play doesn't resume on reload; note in a comment).

### 3. Tests
- `lib/online/worldsService.test.ts`: sp-cloud create **with** profileId succeeds and counts against the profile quota (mixed mp+sp hit the cap together).
- `components/menu/OnlineWorldSelect.test.tsx`: sections split by kind; null-profileId sp row visible under any profile; own-profile sp row visible, other-profile sp row hidden; delete confirm calls the client; cap counts mp+sp owned; `onPlayCloud` fires.
- New e2e `e2e/accountSp.e2e.ts` (or extend cloudSaves): **cross-device journey** — context A: register (per-attempt unique email, keep the tag to reuse), Online Profiles → create profile → "New Singleplayer World" → `waitForGame` → assert `window.__monecraft.net == null` (**no game-server connection**) → place the mid-air Stone marker (cloudSaves pattern) → Save & Quit (unmount push). Context B (fresh, zero localStorage): sign IN with the same email → same profile → Singleplayer card → play → marker block present. Reuses `waitForGame`, marker trick, sign-up helper patterns from `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts`.
- Keep `bun test` unpiped; new PGlite tests `closeTestDb`.

### 4. Docs + CHANGELOG (same PR)
- `docs/online.md`: Identity/account-home bullets (each profile: online worlds AND synced singleplayer worlds; the game server hosts only mp) + the cloud-saves section gains the account-mode create path.
- `docs/manual.md`: "Playing online" — creating singleplayer worlds under a profile; cloud-saves section notes both paths (account-mode native, local upload still works).
- `docs/tuning.md`: `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` wording — counts online **and** singleplayer worlds owned by the profile.
- `docs/testing.md`: coverage rows (service quota test, menu sections, new e2e).
- `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased Added: single-player worlds in account mode — client-side play, per-profile, cloud-synced across devices.

## Commit slices (branch `feat/account-sp-worlds` off `fix/post-identity-followups`)
1. `feat(menu): singleplayer section in the account world list` — OnlineWorldSelect sections/cap/delete + component tests.
2. `feat(shell): play account singleplayer worlds client-side` — GameShell play-cloud path + cache GC.
3. `test(online): sp-cloud worlds share the profile quota` — service test (+ any missed unit coverage).
4. `test(e2e): cross-device account singleplayer journey`.
5. `docs: account-mode singleplayer worlds (+ CHANGELOG)`.

## Verification
- Per commit: `bun run format` + `bun run lint`. Before PR: full gate (`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` unpiped, `build`) + `bun run test:e2e`.
- Manual (pglite dev stack): signed in → profile → New Singleplayer World → network tab shows **no WS**, only `/api/worlds*` fetches; play, quit; second browser signs into the same account → world listed under the profile → continues with the edit present; cap: 10 mixed worlds block both create buttons; hardcore sp death deletes the row.
- After merge: push/PR only on user go-ahead, as usual.

content.content:
## Identity: Local Players and accounts

- **Online play is accounts-only** (email/password via better-auth). There is
  no anonymous-guest layer: an invite link, cloud sync, or hosting all start
  with sign-in/register. Logged-out **Local Players** keep any number of
  browser-local profiles and worlds and make **zero** server calls.
- When signed in, the menu opens into an **account home**
  (`components/menu/AccountProfileSelect.tsx`) listing that account's
  server-side profiles (create/rename/delete, capped at `MAX_ONLINE_PROFILES`,
  synced across devices); picking one shows its online worlds
  (`OnlineWorldSelect`, capped at `MAX_WORLDS_PER_PROFILE` owned worlds), and
  the join ticket carries the profile's name/skin. Worlds joined by invite are
  account-level memberships, so they appear under **every** profile with a
  "Joined" tag.
- Local worlds are **hidden but preserved** while signed in — never deleted,
  never auto-uploaded. The account home's **"Play locally"** button opens the
  local menus without signing out (that's also where cloud-save sync lives);
  "Back to account" returns. Signing out lands on the local flow directly.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.
- The Account panel renders on the profile-select screen **and on the
  first-run create-profile screen** (`components/menu/ProfileSelect.tsx`), so
  sign in / register is reachable before any local profile exists.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves
---
**How it flows through the menu** (all opt-in per world):

- **Upload** — a local world's card gets an "Upload to cloud" action while
  signed in: it creates an `sp-cloud` world row, links it via
  `WorldMeta.cloudId` (a local-manifest field, not part of the save format),
  and pushes the current save. The card then reads "☁ Synced".
- **On another device** — your `sp-cloud` saves you haven't downloaded yet
  appear under **Cloud Saves**; **Download** materializes a local world (linked
  by `cloudId`) and opens it, pulling the blob in.
- **Open** — a cloud-linked world reconciles first (`pullCloudSaveIfNewer`):
  the remote is adopted only when it advanced past this device's sync cursor,
  so a world you played offline keeps its newer local progress instead of being
  overwritten by an older cloud copy. Reuses GameShell's "Opening…" gate.
- **Save** — `useMinecraftGame` mirrors each local autosave/quit up to the
  cloud when the world is `cloudId`-linked and the player is signed in
  (fire-and-forget so the fetch survives the unmount).
